target: PR description (Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Basic.lean generalizations of div_left_injective, div_right_injective, div_left_inj, div_right_inj, div_eq_self, div_eq_inv_self)
claim: The PR generalizes six lemmas from `Group` to `DivInvMonoid` + `IsRightCancelMul` / `DivisionMonoid` + `IsLeftCancelMul`, and with them the Finset and Set lemmas. The description says there is no intended use. The PR names no type that is not a group and carries these classes, so the extra generality has no consumer and buys nothing.
requested_change: Either add to the description a concrete motivating instance or use, meaning a type in Mathlib (or one about to land) that is a cancellative `DivInvMonoid`/`DivisionMonoid` but not a `Group` and that needs these lemmas, or drop the generalization and keep the `Group` statements.
evidence: Searched the base tree for `instance/def ... : DivisionMonoid|DivisionCommMonoid|DivInvMonoid` (24 files). The hits are transfer instances (Opposite, ULift, Prod, Pi, Multiplicative, OrderDual/Lex, Germ, ConjAct). The rest are structures with a zero (GroupWithZero, WithZero, ENNReal, EReal, ℝ, ℂ, Matrix, HahnSeries, Cauchy) or pointwise Set/Finset/Filter, none of them cancellative, and NonemptyInterval/Interval, which have no cancellation instance (a content_search for `Cancel` under Algebra/Order/Interval found none). The `IsRightCancelMul`/`IsCancelMul` instances in the tree are likewise transfer instances (Prod, Opposite, Shrink, Subsemigroup, Additive, hom types, Germ, OrderDual/Lex). So I found no non-group type on which the new statements apply. Zulip (maintainers_only): Kevin Buzzard, 2025-06-19: "generalisation for generalisation's sake with no actual examples can be actively bad for the library because it causes disruption and can slow down typeclass inference"; Yaël Dillies, 2025-08-08: "generality without applicability is merely ruining the soul".

claim: `div_left_injective` is reproved with a three-step manual proof: `intro`, a `have` through `simpa [div_eq_mul_inv]`, then `simpa using mul_right_cancel (a := a₁) (b := b⁻¹) (c := a₂) h'`. A one-line proof works. The PR also deletes the FIXME saying 'this could be by `simpa`' without doing what it says, and adds a needless `: G` ascription to the binder.
requested_change: Write it as `theorem div_left_injective : Function.Injective fun a ↦ a / b := by simpa only [div_eq_mul_inv] using mul_left_injective b⁻¹`. This is the `simpa` form the deleted FIXME asked for, and it keeps the original `fun a ↦ a / b` statement.
evidence: lean_verify_edit on Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Basic.lean, replacing `div_left_injective` with `by simpa only [div_eq_mul_inv] using mul_left_injective b⁻¹` under the PR's `[DivInvMonoid G] [IsRightCancelMul G]`: outcome compiled, no errors. The pre-PR proof (`simp only [div_eq_mul_inv]; exact fun a a' h ↦ mul_left_injective b⁻¹ h`) also compiles unchanged. The simpa bug behind the FIXME is now a regression test in Batteries (`BatteriesTest/simpa.lean`, namespace `div_left_inj_issue`, which proves `div_left_injective` by `simpa only [div_eq_mul_inv] using ...`).

claim: `div_left_inj` is proved by a hand-written iff split: `constructor`, `intro`, a `have` through `simpa`, `simpa using mul_right_cancel ...`, and `rintro rfl; rfl`, the last joining two tactics with `;` on one line. Its mirror `div_right_inj` is the one-term `div_right_injective.eq_iff`, and the same term works here.
requested_change: Replace the proof with `div_left_injective.eq_iff`, i.e. `theorem div_left_inj : b / a = c / a ↔ b = c := div_left_injective.eq_iff`, matching `div_right_inj`. Alternatively keep the pre-PR proof `rw [div_eq_mul_inv, div_eq_mul_inv]; exact mul_left_inj _`, which still compiles.
evidence: lean_verify_edit on Basic.lean with `div_left_inj := div_left_injective.eq_iff`: compiled. The pre-PR proof `rw [div_eq_mul_inv, div_eq_mul_inv]` / `exact mul_left_inj _` also compiled under `[DivInvMonoid G] [IsRightCancelMul G]`. The combined block (all six Basic.lean lemmas with the proofs proposed in these findings) compiled as well.
